ontario_context:
## Ontario (CA-ON)

Ontario fishing is regulated by the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry (MNRF).

- Anglers aged 18-64 need an Outdoors Card plus a valid fishing licence.
- Regulations are zone-based: Ontario is split into 20 Fisheries Management Zones (FMZs). Seasons, limits, and slot sizes vary by zone and by water body.
- The annual Recreational Fishing Regulations Summary published by MNRF is the authoritative reference. Specific water bodies can be checked on Fish ON-Line.
- Border waters with the US (Lake Erie, Huron, Ontario, St. Lawrence River, Lake of the Woods, Rainy Lake) have binational considerations — possession may depend on which side of the line a fish was caught on.
- Indigenous/First Nations waters and reserves are governed separately. If a question concerns those waters, flag it and direct the user to the relevant First Nation's authority.

Use the get_regulations tool to look up actual zone text from the MNRF Recreational Fishing Regulations Summary (parsed from the official PDF). Always remind the user to verify current-year specifics with MNRF before relying on any specific limit, season, or slot size.
